breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet expected in the surf zone. Strong
north to south longshore current expected.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 PM EDT this
evening. For the High Rip Current Risk, from 6 AM EDT this
morning through this evening. For the High Surf Advisory, from

* IMPACTS...Low-lying roads and locations along the Intracoastal
Waterway and adjacent tidal creeks may observe minor coastal
flooding. Check with local officials for any road closures or
impacts. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Affected areas listed are based on
average tide conditions. Additional locations may experience
flooding during periods of heavy rainfall, high winds, or
other factors.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

appropriate action to protect life and property. If travel is

unknown depth.

localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

of southeast Louisiana and southern Mississippi this afternoon.

mid 30 percent range. The 20 ft wind forecast is expected to

weather conditions or at least the effective spread of fires that

restrictions followed.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 23 at 4:16PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
A series of fronts are expected to move across the Interior on
Sunday and Monday. The initial front on Sunday will bring a band
of snowfall across the area. With this first front, light snow
accumulations are expected.

The next front moving across the Interior on Monday will be
accompanied by warmer temperatures, which could bring the
potential for a light rain/snow mix in the valleys and moderate
snow amounts across higher elevations. This could lead to slick
travel conditions, especially during the overnight hours Monday
night into Tuesday when the temperatures could drop below freezing
once again.

Accompanying the second front will be a period of gusty winds
across the higher elevations. This could bring some blowing snow
concerns Monday night/Tuesday morning, which could reduce
visibility to one mile or less.

Stay up to date with the latest forecast by visiting our website,
weather.gov/afg.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 24 at 9:15AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
30W was upgraded to Tropical Storm In-fa over the northern Marshall
Islands at 700 AM ChST this morning, located near 10.6N 166.3E, or
120 miles north-northeast of Ujae Atoll, south of Bikini and Rongelap
Atolls. In-fa has maximum sustained winds of 40 mph, which extend
outward 115 miles to the southeast, 105 miles to the southwest, 100
miles to the northwest, and 40 miles to the northeast. This keeps
Ujae Atoll just outside the direct tropical storm-force wind field,
but strong sustained west to southwest winds with damaging tropical
storm-force gusts are expected through at least tonight as In-fa
begins to meander generally northward. The worst impacts will be
felt for islands and atolls across the northern and central Marshall
Islands, especially for west-facing exposures along the Ralik Chain,
such as Ujae, Enewetak, and Kwajalein Atolls. To the south of In-fa,
expect surging west to southwest winds of 20 to 30 knots with gusts
up to 45 knots, especially near heavier showers or outflow
boundaries. Boats should be safely secured away from west or south-
facing exposures, if possible. Significant boat damage has been
reported along west reefs already.

Seas will be hazardous to small craft throughout much of the central
and northern RMI, and dangerous within the tropical storm-force
winds closer to the center of In-fa. Do not attempt inter-island
travel. Even within the relatively calmer lagoon-side waters, inter-
island travel is strongly discouraged. Passing showers may produce
sudden strong to gale-force gusts, which will create locally
dangerous conditions. West to southwest swells will build to the
south of In- fa through the rest of the weekend, leading to elevated,
potentially hazardous surf along west- and south-facing reefs of the
central and northern RMI, mainly to the north and northwest of
Majuro.

Currently, In-fa is nearly-stationary, with its recent motion showing
a slight southeastward drift at around 1 mph, but is forecast to
begin slowly meandering north-northeast, then north-northwest through
this afternoon. Then, In-fa will see a slight increase in forward
speed through Sunday as it begins to exit the Marshall Islands. Winds
and seas will begin to ease through Sunday night, but sea conditions
may remain hazardous to small craft across the northern Marshalls
through Monday night. Light winds and a drier ridging pattern look to
set up across the region by the end of the week. This situation
will be closely monitored for additional impacts to the Marshall
Islands.

For more information on Tropical Storm In-fa, please refer to
bulletins from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header
WTPN31 PGTW and from the National Weather Service under WMO header
WTPQ31 PGUM.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 22 at 11:30AM MDT until October 25 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Advisory for the following rivers in New Mexico...

San Juan River At Shiprock affecting San Juan County.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...San Juan River at Shiprock.

* WHEN...From this morning to Sunday afternoon.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 12.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 13.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river will fall to 12.0 feet this afternoon. It
will then rise to 12.5 feet this evening. It will fall to 11.9
feet just after midnight tonight. It will then rise to 14.2 feet
Saturday morning. It will fall again and remain below flood
stage.
- Action stage is 13.5 feet.
- Flood stage is 15.5 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you encounter a flooded roadway, turn around and find an
alternative route.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.

NWSheadline: FLOOD ADVISORY IN EFFECT FROM THIS MORNING TO SATURDAY EVENING

properties.areaDesc: Northwest Plateau
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 22 at 11:28AM MDT until October 24 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Albuquerque has issued a Flood
Watch for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Animas River At Farmington affecting Northwest Plateau zone.

* WHAT...Flooding is possible.

* WHERE...Animas River at Farmington.

* WHEN...From Friday evening to Saturday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of the riverwalk in Farmington are
flooded. Local overbank flooding is occurring along the lower
Animas River.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 AM MDT Thursday the stage was 6.4 feet.
- Forecast...Flood stage may be reached late tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 10.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
If you are in the watch area, remain alert to possible flooding.

Residents and those with interests near the river should monitor
rising water levels and be prepared for possible Flood Warnings.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/abq.

The next statement will be issued Friday afternoon at noon MDT.
